turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I noticed a mass in my left breast about four weeks ago, and it’s been rapidly increasing in size. I haven’t had any pain, and there haven’t been any skin or nipple changes.
How old are you, and have you had any recent trauma
I’m 48 years old, and I haven’t had any recent trauma or infections.
Have you or anyone in your family ever had breast cancer or any other breast conditions?
No, I don’t have any family history of breast cancer or other breast conditions. I also haven’t had anything like this before.
Have you noticed any other symptoms like fever, weight loss,
I haven’t had any fever, weight loss, night sweats, or changes in my appetite. The main issue is the rapidly growing mass in my left breast, and I’ve had no pain and no skin or nipple changes.
Are you currently taking any hormone replacement therapy,
I’m not currently taking any hormone replacement therapy. I also haven’t been on other hormone medications to my knowledge.
Can you describe how the mass feels
It feels like a distinct lump in my left breast, and it seems firmer than the surrounding tissue. It has gotten larger quickly over the past four weeks, but it isn’t tender or painful.
Have you noticed any swelling or lumps under your armpit
Patient: I haven’t noticed any swelling or lumps under my armpit on the left or right side.
Does the size of the mass seem to change with your menstrual cycle?
I don’t think it changes with my menstrual cycle—I’ve mainly noticed it enlarging steadily over the past four weeks.
When was your last mammogram, and were
Patient: I’ve never had a mammogram before. I don’t recall ever being told I needed one.
Have you noticed any discharge from your nipple, or any changes
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any nipple discharge. I also haven’t seen any changes to the nipple itself beyond finding the lump in the left breast.
Does the mass feel like it can be moved around under the skin, or does it feel firmly attached to the skin or

It feels like a distinct lump that’s firmer than the surrounding tissue, and I think it can move a little under the skin rather than feeling rigidly fixed to it. I haven’t noticed any skin dimpling or pulling over the area.
Have you ever been pregnant or breastfed, and
I’ve been pregnant before, but I haven’t breastfed. I don’t have any history of similar breast issues during or after pregnancy.
